title: Single-Rod Bead Manipulation (0–9)
subtitle: Learn how to set beads, with notes on using a physical soroban.
challenge: Which fingers should you use to set the number 6 on a single rod in a single swift motion?
predictionPrompt: How do you set 6 in standard Japanese Soroban fingering?

predictionOptions.label: Push lower bead then upper bead with index finger
Pinch thumb and index finger together toward the beam

formalDefinition: Standard fingering: thumb pushes lower beads up (+1 to +4); index finger pulls lower beads down (-1 to -4); index finger moves upper bead down (+5) and up (-5). Digits 6-9 use a simultaneous pinch.

steps: Simultaneously bring 1 upper bead down and 1 lower bead up with a pinch.

misconception.mistake: Using the index finger to push lower beads up.
misconception.correction: The thumb has greater tactile strength and ergonomic speed for upward pushes.

reflection: Consistent fingering creates muscle memory, which later enables rapid mental abacus (Anzan) calculation.
prerequisiteCheck: There are four lower beads and one upper bead per rod. Legal engaged lower beads form a contiguous group touching the bar.
representation: Digits 0–4 use that many lower beads; digits 5–9 use the upper bead plus 0–4 lower beads. Thus 7 uses 5 + 2.

faded.prompt: Complete the setting for 8: upper bead __; lower beads engaged __. For 4: upper __; lower __.
faded.solution: 8: upper engaged, 3 lower. 4: upper away, 4 lower.

independent.solution: 0: all away; 5: upper only; 9: upper and all 4 lower.

independent.prompt: Can a legal rod use five lower beads to show 5?
independent.solution: No. It has only four lower beads. Use the upper bead to show 5.

explanation: Explain how one upper/four lower beads provide exactly ten digit states without counting beads away from the bar.

transfer.prompt: Read a physical instrument in which the upper bead is away and two lower beads touch the bar, then explain how keyboard controls can represent the same state.
transfer.solution: The rod digit is 2. The equivalent logical state is upper=false, lower=2. This describes value; it does not assess a physical finger technique.

retrieval: Tomorrow set/read 6, 2, 9 in random order. After a week, describe the change from 9 to 4.
reviewNote: Expanded prototype lesson. Independent mathematical, pedagogical, and accessibility review is pending.
